content: 1. Digoxin Dose Adjustment: When co-administering digoxin with other drugs, consider reducing the digoxin dose by approximately 30-50% or modifying the dosing frequency. Close monitoring is essential. 2. Ivabradine and Digoxin: These drugs can enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor closely, as the combination increases the risk of bradycardia, especially when used with other heart rate-lowering agents like beta-blockers or amiodarone. 3. Ivacaftor and Digoxin: Ivacaftor increases digoxin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely, as systemic exposure to digoxin may increase significantly. 4. Ketoconazole and Digoxin: Ketoconazole raises digoxin levels by inhibiting P-gp. Monitor closely and use caution. 5. Ketoprofen, Ketorolac, and Digoxin: These drugs increase serum potassium levels. Monitor closely and use caution to avoid hyperkalemia. 6. Labetalol and Digoxin: Labetalol enhances the effects of digoxin through pharmacodynamic synergy and increases serum potassium. Monitor closely and use caution. 7. Lansoprazole and Digoxin: Lansoprazole increases digoxin toxicity by raising gastric pH, which applies only to oral forms. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Lapatinib and Digoxin: Lapatinib increases digoxin levels via P-gp inhibition. Monitor closely and use caution. 9. Lasmiditan and Digoxin: Lasmiditan raises digoxin levels through P-gp inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir and Digoxin: This combination increases digoxin levels via P-gp inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 11. Lenacapavir and Digoxin: Lenacapavir affects hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing digoxin levels. Use caution and monitor therapeutic concentrations. 12. Leniolisib and Digoxin: Leniolisib, an OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 inhibitor, may increase systemic exposure to digoxin. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 13. Levacetylleucine and Digoxin: Levacetylleucine inhibits P-gp, potentially increasing digoxin levels. Monitor closely, though the clinical significance is not fully characterized. 14. Digoxin and Levalbuterol: Digoxin increases serum potassium, while levalbuterol decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor closely. 15. Levofloxacin and Digoxin: Levofloxacin increases digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Levothyroxine and Digoxin: Levothyroxine reduces digoxin's effects through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Licorice and Digoxin: Licorice enhances digoxin's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 18. Lily of the Valley and Digoxin: This combination increases toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. It is contraindicated. 19. Linezolid and Digoxin: Linezolid increases digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Liothyronine and Digoxin: Liothyronine reduces digoxin's effects through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Liraglutide and Digoxin: Liraglutide decreases digoxin levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 22. Lisinopril and Digoxin: Lisinopril increases digoxin levels through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Lomitapide and Digoxin: Lomitapide increases digoxin levels via P-gp inhibition. Consider reducing the digoxin dose and monitor closely. 24. Lomustine and Digoxin: Lomustine decreases digoxin levels by impairing absorption due to mucositis or stomatitis. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 25. Lonafarnib and Digoxin: Lonafarnib, a weak P-gp inhibitor, increases digoxin levels. Monitor for adverse reactions and reduce the digoxin dose if needed. 26. Loratadine and Digoxin: Loratadine increases digoxin levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Lornoxicam and Digoxin: Both drugs increase serum potassium. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Losartan and Digoxin: Both drugs increase serum potassium. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor and Digoxin: Lumacaftor can both inhibit and induce P-gp, potentially affecting digoxin levels. Monitor closely. 30. Magnesium Salts and Digoxin: Digoxin decreases magnesium levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 31. Mavorixafor and Digoxin: Mavorixafor, a P-gp inhibitor, increases digoxin levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Meclizine and Digoxin: Meclizine increases digoxin levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 33. Methotrexate and Digoxin: Methotrexate reduces digoxin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Monitor closely and adjust the digoxin dose if necessary. 34. Metoprolol and Digoxin: Metoprolol enhances digoxin's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy and increases serum potassium. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the risk of bradycardia. 35. Metronidazole and Digoxin: Metronidazole increases digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Midodrine and Digoxin: Digoxin increases midodrine levels through competition for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Miglitol and Digoxin: Miglitol decreases digoxin levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 38. Mineral Oil and Digoxin: Mineral oil reduces digoxin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Minocycline and Digoxin: Minocycline increases digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Mirabegron and Digoxin: Mirabegron increases digoxin levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Moexipril and Digoxin: Moexipril increases digoxin levels through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Moxifloxacin and Digoxin: Moxifloxacin increases digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Nabumetone and Digoxin: Both drugs increase serum potassium. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Nadolol and Digoxin: Nadolol enhances digoxin's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy and increases serum potassium. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the risk of bradycardia. 45. Nafcillin and Digoxin: Nafcillin increases digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Naproxen and Digoxin: Both drugs increase serum potassium. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Nebivolol and Digoxin: Nebivolol enhances digoxin's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy and increases serum potassium. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the risk of bradycardia. 48. Nefazodone and Digoxin: Nefazodone increases digoxin levels via P-gp inhibition. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 49. Neomycin and Digoxin: Neomycin alters intestinal flora, reducing digoxin absorption. This applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Neratinib and Digoxin: Neratinib increases digoxin levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Nicardipine and Digoxin: Nicardipine increases digoxin levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Nifedipine and Digoxin: Nifedipine increases digoxin levels by reducing clearance, raising the risk of toxicity. Adjust the digoxin dose as needed. 53. Nilotinib and Digoxin: Nilotinib increases digoxin levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir and Digoxin: This combination increases digoxin levels via P-gp inhibition. Measure serum digoxin concentrations before initiating therapy, reduce the digoxin dose by 30-50%, and monitor closely during co-administration.
